text.en:
Currency Act 1967
Currency
(Denominations and Characteristics of Coins)
Notification 2022
Pursuant to section 17(5) of the Currency Act 1967, it is notified for general information that the denominations and characteristics of the coins to be issued on 1 January 2023 by the Monetary Authority of Singapore are as shown in the Schedule.

THE SCHEDULE
Description of the 2023 Chinese Almanac Coins
(Year of the Rabbit) to be issued on 1 January 2023

$2

Nickel-plated 99% Zinc

Round

Milled
Design of Obverse
1.The background of the $2 silver proof‑like colour coin and the $2 nickel‑plated zinc proof‑like coin is shiny silver.
2.The Singapore Coat of Arms is engraved in the centre of the coin with the year‑date “2023” below it.
3.The word “SINGAPORE” appears once in each of the 4 official languages and is engraved on the coin around the Singapore Coat of Arms.
Design of Reverse
1.The background of the $2 silver proof‑like colour coin and the $2 nickel‑plated zinc proof‑like coin is shiny silver.
2.The $2 silver proof‑like colour coin and the $2 nickel‑plated zinc proof‑like coin share a common design which features —
(a)a rabbit in the centre of the foreground leaping forward, with its left ear and head partially covering the Amber Beacon Tower, both forelegs on the grass, with its body and both hindlegs partially covering the sea and the Bedok Jetty;
(b)the Bedok Jetty in the background on the left side of the coin;
(c)the Amber Beacon Tower with a breakwater rock structure behind the Amber Beacon Tower in the background on the right side of the coin;
(d)plants in the foreground on the left side of the coin below the 2 hindlegs of the rabbit; and
(e)the denomination “$2” engraved and placed at 12 o’clock, above the rabbit.
3.The weight in troy oz and fineness of the coin are engraved above the rabbit of the $2 silver proof‑like colour coin.
4.The rabbit featured in the $2 silver proof‑like colour coin is in colour.

Design of Obverse
1.The background of the $5 silver proof coin and the $5 silver proof colour coin is shiny silver.
2.The background of the $5 gold brilliant uncirculated coin is shiny gold.
3.The Singapore Coat of Arms is engraved in the centre of the coin with the year‑date “2023” below it.
4.The word “SINGAPORE” appears once in each of the 4 official languages and is engraved on the coin around the Singapore Coat of Arms.
5.The mintmark is engraved on the coin around the Singapore Coat of Arms at 5 o’clock for the $5 silver proof coin and the $5 silver proof colour coin.
Design of Reverse
1.The background of the $5 silver proof coin and the $5 silver proof colour coin is shiny silver.
2.The background of the $5 gold brilliant uncirculated coin is shiny gold.
3.The $5 silver proof coin and the $5 silver proof colour coin share a common design which features —
(a)a rabbit in the centre of the foreground leaping forward, with its left ear and head partially covering the Amber Beacon Tower, both forelegs on the grass, with its body and both hindlegs partially covering the sea and the Bedok Jetty;
(b)the Bedok Jetty in the background on the left side of the coin;
(c)the Amber Beacon Tower with a breakwater rock structure behind the Amber Beacon Tower in the background on the right side of the coin;
(d)plants in the foreground on the left side of the coin below the 2 hindlegs of the rabbit; and
(e)the denomination “$5” engraved and placed at 12 o’clock, above the rabbit.
4.The rabbit featured in the $5 silver proof colour coin is in colour.
5.The $5 gold brilliant uncirculated coin features —
(a)a rabbit engraved in the centre;
(b)the denomination “$5” engraved and placed at 6 o’clock, below the rabbit; and
(c)the weight in grams and fineness of the coin, engraved and placed at 12 o’clock, above the rabbit.

(b)the Bedok Jetty by the sea in the background, and a breakwater rock structure and a palm tree in the middle ground on the left side of the coin;
(c)the Amber Beacon Tower with a breakwater rock structure behind the Amber Beacon Tower in the background on the right side of the coin;
(d)plants in the foreground on both the left and right sides of the coin;
(e)the denomination “$80” engraved and placed at 9 o’clock, to the left of the rabbit, partially covering a palm tree and the Bedok Jetty; and
